newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian debt holds a narrow range, slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Australian debt holds a narrow range, slow trade.

text.p: *Australian bond yields held a narrow trading range during a slow morning session, in sharp contrast to Friday's stinging rally after the Reserve Bank eased policy.

Australian bond yields held a narrow trading range during a slow morning session, in sharp contrast to Friday's stinging rally after the Reserve Bank eased official rates by 0.5 percentage points to 5.50 percent.
"The market is trying to find its feet after Friday. I think we are going to see a couple of days of consolidation," one trader at a local bank said.
The thin conditions also reflected the U.S. holiday for Memorial Day and there was no trading in U.S. Treasuries during Asian trading.

Traders said the market was expect to find support on any retracement to the low-92.300's on the June 10-year bond futures contract and that the market held up reasonably well in light of profit-taking by offshore accounts late on Friday.
U.S. Treasuries finished Friday's pre-holiday shortened session modestly higher in price before the long holiday weekend.

The local market faces a steady flow of data this week, including key components of the next week's first quarter GDP, but they are somewhat overshadowed with the rate cut in place. At this stage, the cut is seen as the last in the cycle.

Long-dated spreads were little changed against the dollar bloc after narrowing sharply on Friday after the rate cut. Canadian debt was little changed on Friday, while N.Z. bond yields were a touch higher during a fairly illiquid opening.
Local bond yield curve continues to steepen.
